systems.name: Progressively flattened spiral stack
systems.status: visually-confirmed pattern; procedural interpretation; source bounds proposed
systems.explanation: A shared spiral contour repeats down a column; vertical extent and pitch grow together.
invariants: Spiral topology remains constant.
Row extents follow a declared geometric progression.

systems.name: Ordered wave-line field
systems.status: visually-confirmed pattern; procedural interpretation; source bounds proposed
systems.explanation: The ECAL source bends an ordered family of lines into a flow field. This prototype preserves shared phase and row order; its printed arrows and exact local flow are not recovered.
invariants: Every row samples the same smooth displacement field.
Stroke width scales in physical canvas units.

systems.name: Four-way reflected arc bundles
systems.status: visually-confirmed pattern; procedural interpretation; source bounds proposed
systems.explanation: The VOLUMES reference reflects curved stroke bundles across both axes, producing a central counterform. Smooth opposing arc bundles are a declared interpretation.
invariants: Four quadrants share one generating curve family.
Horizontal and vertical reflection and bundle count remain explicit.

systems.name: Affine zigzag tile field
systems.status: visually-confirmed pattern; procedural interpretation; source bounds proposed
systems.explanation: The red-and-black source repeats a slanted tile on a regular lattice. The prototype isolates the affine repeat from photographed shading and wall context.
invariants: All tiles share a polygon and lattice spacing.
Row and column counts control density independently.

systems.name: Repeated satellite-circle clusters
systems.status: visually-confirmed pattern; procedural interpretation; source bounds proposed
systems.explanation: The Cully source distributes small circle clusters across a repeated field. This interpretation shares one cluster construction and cycles its orientation.
invariants: Each cluster contains one body and two attached satellite circles.
Cluster orientation follows a repeatable index cycle.

systems.name: Perforated rounded-tile lattice
systems.status: visually-confirmed pattern; procedural interpretation; source bounds proposed
systems.explanation: The Festival de la Cité source combines rounded masses and circular counters on a repeated lattice. The prototype isolates that topology; the full multicolor composition is not reconstructed.
invariants: Counters remain negative space inside each tile.
Hole count and lattice density are independent controls.

systems.name: Equal-angle radial spokes
systems.status: visually-confirmed pattern; procedural interpretation; source bounds proposed
systems.explanation: The FOCUS icon sheet contains a radial line motif. The prototype explicitly repeats a segment at equal angular intervals.
invariants: Angular increments equal 360 degrees divided by spoke count.
Inner and outer radii remain common to every spoke.

systems.name: Shared-petal rotational rosette
systems.status: visually-confirmed pattern; procedural interpretation; source bounds proposed
systems.explanation: The FOCUS icon sheet repeats four pointed oval petals about one center. A shared closed Bézier petal supplies an editable rotational rule.
invariants: Every petal is a rigid rotation of one closed path.
Petal count, width and phase remain independent parameters.

systems.name: Disc wreath
systems.status: SAM-refined source; visually reviewed vector interpretation
systems.explanation: Equal circular modules occupy an elliptical orbit at equal angular intervals. Radius is limited to keep neighboring discs separate and inside the field.
invariants: Centers share one orbit and equal angular spacing.
Module radius stays constant; a chord bound prevents collisions.

systems.name: Segmented ring
systems.status: SAM-refined source; visually reviewed vector interpretation
systems.explanation: Disjoint annular sectors share inner and outer circles. Segment count, angular coverage and band thickness vary independently.
invariants: All sectors share the same two radii.
An angular gap separates every neighboring sector.

systems.name: Polygon contours
systems.status: SAM-refined source; visually reviewed vector interpretation
systems.explanation: A regular polygon supplies one frame or a family of concentric contours. Side count changes the primitive; equal radial steps and capped stroke width preserve nested gaps.
invariants: Every contour shares side count, center and orientation.
Stroke width is capped below the contour separation.

systems.name: Star frame
systems.status: SAM-refined source; visually reviewed vector interpretation
systems.explanation: Alternating tip and root radii define an even star. A concentric scaled star is subtracted with even-odd fill; zero aperture produces a solid star.
invariants: Tips repeat at equal angular intervals.
The inner and outer stars are homothetic and never cross.

systems.name: Notched disc
systems.status: SAM-refined source; visually reviewed vector interpretation
systems.explanation: A triangular wedge removes part of a disc. The cut can reach its center or stop short; orientation and flattening transform the complete cut silhouette.
invariants: One circular boundary and one wedge define the primitive.
Subtraction is clipped to the disc, so no wedge exterior is printed.

systems.name: Radial cell mosaic
systems.status: SAM-refined source; visually reviewed vector interpretation
systems.explanation: Shared concentric band boundaries are partitioned into staggered curved cells. Cell count increases with radius; seeded seam and boundary variations retain the radial organization observed in the source.
invariants: Adjacent bands use the same boundary function.
Cell separation leaves real negative-space gutters.
The declared seed reproduces every irregular boundary.

note: SigLIP shortlisted sources across 1,130 frozen posters. A coding-agent visual review selected eight transferable shape relationships. These are editable vector interpretations, not automatic layer recovery, calibrated detections or exact source reconstructions. No type geometry is used. Six SAM-refined source interpretations share the shape-library vector renderers. SAM model estimates are not detection-accuracy probabilities.
